summary: Frontend-only E2E of the Journey Codebook package via Playwright on the public preview URL. Walked the full 5-step wizard (new quant study -> step labels -> NEW step 3 'ลงรหัสปัญหา'), pasted 5 Thai interviews, extracted candidates, verified verbatim quotes + interview index, renamed/approved/rejected rows, confirmed activation gates block with Thai reasons, activated codebook v1, published, completed a full public respondent run (approved category ids + 'อื่น ๆ' + nomination cap), verified the owner dashboard provenance/other-rate/saturation/reliability cards, back-coded the free text (rate 0% -> 50%), verified the qualitative-audit card with a Mermaid-seeded second study, and re-verified the pre-existing demo study (140 responses, Mermaid map, all tables, library_default warning) plus its public link. All test data purged: demo-journey-kafae-001 is back at EXACTLY 140 responses, 0 TEST_QA studies, 0 codebooks, 0 leftover drafts.

minor.issue: Thai pain cues are matched as plain substrings, so 'วนอยู่หลายรอบ' matched the cue 'รอ' (waiting) and that sentence was attached as a verbatim quote to the 'รอคิวนาน' candidate — a false-positive verbatim under the wrong category. Also the default label of every candidate is the whole sentence and a near-duplicate row ('… · นาน') is produced, so the student must rename every row manually.

ui_bugs.issue: Queue item shows the raw state id as the step label: 'ขั้น s1' instead of the Thai step label (labelOf). Raw ID leaks into owner-facing copy.
The 'ดูรายเส้นทาง' detail table prints raw state ids in the from/to columns (rendered 's1  s2') instead of Thai step labels.

data-testids are keyed on response_id only, so a respondent who writes 'อื่น ๆ' on two steps produces duplicate ids: two bc-item-<response_id>, eight bc-cat-<response_id>-<cid> (4 categories x 2 rows) and two bc-apply-<response_id>. Internal state key already uses response_id|state_id — the testids should too. Functionality still worked (pending 2 -> 1).
data-testid 'journey-provenance-line' is rendered twice on the same page (lines 456 and 575), so the selector is ambiguous.

'เปิดใช้ชุดรหัสนี้' is enabled on first load before any blockers are known, so the first click can fail with a server error instead of being prevented; blockers only appear after 'บันทึกและตรวจ'. Once saved the behaviour is correct (button disabled + full Thai reason list).
After successful activation the wizard jumps straight to step 4, so the 'ใช้ชุดรหัสเวอร์ชัน 1 อยู่' confirmation card (cb-active) is never seen unless the user navigates back to step 3.

issues: No contrast/spacing problems found; warnings render in the red jy-warn band and are readable
Tables and the Mermaid map render at 1920px without overflow

action_items: Replace raw state ids with Thai step labels in the back-coding queue ('ขั้น s1') and in the qualitative-audit detail table (from/to columns).
Make back-coding data-testids unique per (response_id, state_id) so a respondent with two 'อื่น ๆ' texts does not create duplicate testids.
Render 'journey-provenance-line' only once per dashboard page (or give the second instance its own testid).
Optional: fetch blockers on codebook-step load so cb-activate starts disabled with reasons already visible.
Optional: tighten the Thai cue matcher (word-boundary / negative list) so 'รอบ' does not match the 'รอ' cue, and seed shorter default candidate labels.
critical_code_review_comments: JourneyBackCoding.jsx L92-L105: keyOf(it) already combines response_id|state_id for state; the data-testid should use the same key. Duplicate DOM testids make the queue untestable and ambiguous for screen readers.
JourneyProvenance.jsx rows(): e.from / e.to are state ids; pass the study's label map into QualitativeAuditCard and render label_th.
JourneyDashboardPage.jsx L456 & L575: same data-testid used twice.

Verified (no action): patchRow (wizard) and toggleCat/setPainDetail (respondent) are functional updaters — rapid double toggling kept the correct final state, so the two lost-update fixes hold. No TDZ white screen on the respondent page; no console errors anywhere in the run.
seed_data_creation: Created and then PURGED two temp studies (TEST_QA_CJM_Codebook b81b7ae7-…, TEST_QA_CJM_Audit 4182e889-…) and withdrew the one demo response submitted (token 9b9d5329…). Verified afterwards: demo-journey-kafae-001 = 140 responses, journey_codebooks = 0, TEST_QA studies = 0, journey_response_drafts = 0.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Login must be done with page.type (not fill) plus a ~1.2s wait after the login form appears, otherwise the email field stays empty. Wizard step navigation uses the shared Stepper testids be-step-0..4 (there is no journey-step-* clickable). Replay screen confirm button is jy-replay-confirm. Respondent flow order: consent -> episode -> (subject) -> checklist -> first -> branch(jy-branch-conv ends) -> replay -> grid -> pain -> paindepth -> outcome -> segments. The qualitative-audit card only renders when the codebook carries claimed edges, i.e. Mermaid code was pasted in the codebook step (verified working). Saturation/reliability/back-coding cards are hidden for the library_default demo study by design. Always purge created studies and withdraw demo responses; delete leftover rows in journey_response_drafts too.
rca_of_the_issue: Both raw-id leaks come from components that receive ids without the study's label map: JourneyBackCoding prints it.state_id directly and QualitativeAuditCard prints e.from/e.to from edge_coverage output. The duplicate testids come from keying DOM attributes on response_id while the component's own state key is response_id|state_id — one respondent can produce several queue rows.
